question: How can a multi-candidate tournament for coding agents convert more failures into solves?

brief.note: Brief: how to make the tournament convert more failures into solves; scope = LLM code candidates, verifiers, diversity; budget 25 searches/45 min.

landscape.note: Landscape: three levers named (diversity, selection method, feedback loop) plus the bias ceiling.

plan.note: Plan: Q2 diversity papers, Q4 selection scoring, Q3 refinement, Q5 bias/variance; primary abstracts read.

depth.note: Depth: four primary abstracts read in full; quotes captured for C1-C5.

midpoint.note: Midpoint: all five threads have at least one primary source; enough to answer.

edges.note: Edges: no evidence found that a scalar self-judge closes the pass@N gap; the bias plateau is the boundary.

verify.note: Verify: every claim carries a primary source with an exact quote.

report.note: Redteam: would be falsified if cross-candidate joint scoring failed to beat isolated scores on code tasks; no such evidence found.

sources.title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation

claims.statement: Parallel sampling is limited by diversity collapse: models concentrate on a few modes and repeated samples repeat the same mistakes; allocating compute across modes improves scaling and the attainable Pass@k.
claims.quote: its effectiveness is sharply limited by diversity collapse, where models concentrate on a few modes and repeated samples produce the same mistakes

claims.statement: A training-free prompt that asks the model to verbalize a distribution over responses raises output diversity by 1.6-2.1x in creative writing.
claims.quote: in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting

claims.statement: Scoring candidates jointly rather than one at a time improves verification by up to 7 percentage points and reaches the same peak accuracy at 17-42% lower cost.
claims.quote: Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding that baseline's peak accuracy with 17-42% lower inference cost

claims.statement: More selection compute reduces variance but the ranking bias plateaus, which is why adding candidates does not reliably close the gap to pass@N.
claims.quote: additional compute reduces variance, while bias initially decreases before approaching a plateau

claims.statement: One model can iteratively refine its own output with self-feedback and gain about 20 points on average across seven tasks, without extra training.
claims.quote: improving by ~20% absolute on average in task performance
